questions.question: According to the speaker, what happens to the net export function when the exchange rate is depreciated?
questions.explanation: The primary excerpt states that depreciating the exchange rate moves the net export function up (Q0000).
questions.topic: Effect of exchange‑rate depreciation on net exports

evidence.quote:
And given my assumption, when you depreciate the exchange rate,
 then it moves the net export function up.

original_segments.text: And given my assumption, when you depreciate the exchange rate,
then it moves the net export function up.
Now, the problem is that if you do that,
that's also going to be expansionary,
because now you had certain equilibrium level of output,
And now, there's going to be expenditures switching all
around the world towards your goods.
So you're going to end up producing more.
And so suppose that you didn't want that extra production.
You just wanted to fix your trade balance.
Then you have to set that.
And that's what I've done here.
That's very typical.
Suppose you're in a situation where you have a very
large trade deficit, but you're OK with the collision
level of output you have.
And a typical package is you depreciate your currency, but
you also reduce government expenditure, OK?
Because the position of the currency is expansionary.
It's expansionary.
It improves the trade deficit, but it's also expansionary,
because you relocate expenditure
both of residents and foreigners towards your good.

questions.answer: Because it shifts expenditures of residents and foreigners toward domestic goods.
